title: permanent_bipedal3 single-u64 fast path
description:
Implement `permanent_bipedal3` for $n \le 64$: the single-`u64`-pair fast path that uses `Bipedal3` arithmetic, walks `gray_code_iter`, and updates a single `Bipedal3` column-sum word in-place per step.

## Background

For $n \le 64$, the column-sum vector fits in a single `Bipedal3` (one `u64` pair). Each Gray-code step is then a single `Bipedal3::add` or `Bipedal3::sub` against the toggled column (also a single `Bipedal3`). The reduction at each step is `Bipedal3::fold_mul` (inherent on the value, paper Theorem 2.1).

This is the headline single-thread fast path. SIMD batching across multiple matrices (T12) and multi-word streaming for $n > 64$ (T14) extend this baseline; both consume `permanent_bipedal3` as the inner kernel.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `gf2-algebra::permanent::permanent_bipedal3(matrix: &Bipedal3Matrix) -> Fp<3>` exists, requires `matrix.cols() == matrix.rows()` and `matrix.cols() <= 64`.
- [ ] [hard] Implementation walks `gray_code_iter(n)`, updates a single `Bipedal3` column-sum in-place via `add`/`sub`, and folds via the bipedal multiplication tree.
- [ ] [hard] Output bit-identical to `permanent_ryser<Fp<3>>` (T7) on 1000 random matrices for each $n \in \{1, \ldots, 16\}$ and 100 random matrices for $n \in \{20, 24, 28, 32\}$.
- [ ] [hard] No `unsafe` (per the crate's `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`).
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes; large-$n$ correctness tests complete under 5 s each (the 32 case at ~$2^{32}$ ops fits the budget on the dev host without `--ignored`).
